_about: Hand-curated trial batch of discovery points of interest (Queen West, Trinity-Bellwoods, Kensington-Chinatown), November 17, 2026. Candidates came from out/*.csv (OpenStreetMap) and the City's StrollTO; each entry was checked against the sources listed. 'why' lines are our own words. 'quote' is the City's text, used with credit under the Open Government Licence - Toronto. Kinds and lenses follow the project's discovery brief. Businesses need only to be open and of their place: a story is optional (a 'why' can just say what the place is), and only national and multinational megachains are left out, so small local chains are in. Each place's 'checked' is the day its details were last confirmed against its sources (YYYY-MM-DD); a page can show it as "last checked". Status is as of that date; nothing here is published.

places.name: Graffiti Alley (Rush Lane)
places.why: About a kilometre of laneway south of Queen West, between Spadina and Portland, covered in street art. Rick Mercer walked it for the rants on the Rick Mercer Report (2004–2018).

quote.text: Toronto's famous Graffiti Alley holds multiple murals to explore on the walls of Rush Lane.

places.name: Trinity Bellwoods Park and the Lovebot white squirrel mural
places.why: The park was once Trinity College's campus; the 1904 gates still stand on Queen. It sits on the buried Garrison Creek and is home to the neighbourhood's famous white squirrels.

quote.text: The university opened to students on January 15, 1852. Of the original campus, only the St. Hilda's women's residence (now the John Gibson House for seniors) and the entrance gates (constructed in 1904) remain standing.

places.name: Kensington Market Garden Car
places.why: An old car turned into a planter at Oxford and Augusta. It's the second car to do the job, and it's taken away in winter.

quote.text: Not many know that this is the second car used for this installation. The first was created in 2006 by a now-inactive community group, Streets Are for People.

places.name: Sonic Boom
places.why: Billed as Canada's largest independent record store. It started in the Annex, spent years in the Honest Ed's building, and moved to this 13,000-square-foot Spadina space in 2014.
places.notes: The Scott Pilgrim cameo was at an earlier location, so the seen-on-screen lens doesn't apply to this address.

places.name: The Beguiling
places.why: Comics and graphic-novel shop founded on Harbord Street in 1987, later in a house beside Honest Ed's, and on College since 2017. Its staff started the Toronto Comic Arts Festival in 2003.

places.name: Rotate This
places.why: Opened on Queen West in 1991, a few weeks after Nirvana's Nevermind came out. Moved to Ossington in 2016 and still sells tickets to indie shows.

places.name: Grasshopper Records
places.why: Vinyl shop opened in 2012 by musician Derek "Grasshopper" Madison. It stays open until about midnight, so you can buy a record after a show.

places.name: Type Books
places.why: Independent bookshop opened across from Trinity Bellwoods Park in April 2006, when many indie bookstores were closing. It was founded by two Canadian literature PhDs.

places.name: Sanagan's Meat Locker
places.why: Whole-animal butcher selling meat from Ontario family farms. It opened in 2009 in the space of Max & Son, a market butcher for 54 years, and in 2012 moved into the former European Meats shop.

places.name: Global Cheese
places.why: Second-generation family cheese shop in the market since July 1, 1970. Look for the cow statues and the free samples.
places.notes: Founding date comes from the shop's own listing (via an Airbnb page). Confirm on the shop's website before publishing.

places.name: Blackbird Baking Co.
places.why: Sourdough and baguette bakery. Simon Blackwell, a fourth-generation baker, began in a shared kitchen in 2011 and opened this first shop in 2014.

places.name: Black Market Vintage
places.why: Punk-era vintage store that began in 1980 as pop-up shops to pay the founder's way through school. Known for "$10 or less". Its famous basement at 256 Queen closed in 2019, and the store moved across the street.
places.osm_stale: node/1358246287 (256 Queen St W, the old basement)
places.notes: Needs a point at 347 Queen St W. The OSM node is the old location.

places.name: White Squirrel Coffee Shop
places.why: Named after the white squirrels of Trinity Bellwoods Park across the street. Neighbours treat them as a local legend.
places.notes: Opening year not found in any source. Pairs with the White Squirrel sculpture nearby (OSM node/10858983186).

places.name: Sam James Coffee Bar (Ossington)
places.why: Part of a small Toronto coffee bar chain. Sam James opened his first one on Harbord in 2009 and roasts his own beans (Cut Coffee).
places.notes: About 5 locations. The Harbord original (University neighbourhood) has the founding story.

places.name: Moonbean Coffee Company
places.why: Long-running Kensington café that roasts its coffee in-house.
places.notes: No dated source for its founding year.

checked_and_dropped.name: Dufflet Pastries
checked_and_dropped.reason: Queen West café closed April 2023; the bakery is now wholesale only (OSM still lists it).

checked_and_dropped.name: Craft Ontario Shop
checked_and_dropped.reason: 1106 Queen St W closed at the end of July 2026; new home at 401 Richmond St W from August 2027 (OSM still lists it).

checked_and_dropped.name: Black Market - Downstairs
checked_and_dropped.reason: The 256 Queen St W basement closed in 2019; the store moved to 347 Queen St W (kept above, needs a new point).

checked_and_dropped.name: BMV Books (Queen West)
checked_and_dropped.reason: Unclear: this store closed in January 2020, and a September 2026 report says BMV operates at 244 Queen W again, with ABC Books moving in. Check in person or by phone before including.
